output.review_comment:
I'm requesting changes, but only because the docstring is now out of date. The code itself looks correct.

The code works. I traced all 9 tests against the new logic and they pass. Checking `word[1:]` keeps "iPhone", "NASA" and "McKinsey" as written, including when they are the first word ("iPhone Photography…"). Small words are now handled correctly as the first word, the last word, and with trailing punctuation ("come in, sit down" → "Come in, Sit Down"). The earlier bug is gone: the old code lowercased mixed-case words and never capitalized a small last word.

What needs fixing: the new after-colon rule contradicts the docstring. The teammate said the tests encode the spec agreed with the editorial team, so the rule itself is right: capitalizing the first word of a subtitle is standard headline style. But the docstring still says a small word is capitalized only when it's the first or last word of the whole text. So the documentation now describes something the function doesn't do. The agent pointed out this conflict but left it unresolved, and the PR description says the rule was added "only so that `test_subtitle_after_colon` passes." It's the right behavior, but it isn't documented.

Before merging:
1. Update the docstring: in rule 2, add that a small word is also capitalized when the previous word ends with ":" (the start of a subtitle).
2. Replace the PR description: it currently reads like a chat reply ("Perfect! ✅"). It should say what changed and that the after-colon rule comes from the agreed editorial spec.

Once the docstring matches, this is ready to merge.
